authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Turner groups Lahnda hekk/hikk, Punjabi ikk/hekka, northwestern akh/yakh, Oriya eka and Gujarati ek/eko in the retained-k ēkka branch. These simple survey numerals, including both Awankari ekʰ/īka alternatives, match that family with regional vowels, aspiration and inflection. Turner leaves emphatic doubling versus early Sanskrit reborrowing unresolved; this link does not resolve that prehistoric alternative.

proposals.evidence: Turner lists Awankari dā, Oriya dasa and daś throughout Western Pahari under daśa ten. The survey responses match those regional numeral stems, with local vowel, sibilant and aspiration variation; both Awankari alternatives are the same form. The separate dā/das response is excluded because Turner marks Punjabi das as a Hindi loan.

proposals.evidence: Turner records Oriya sa/sae, Western Pahari śau and Gujarati sɔ in the śata hundred family. These whole survey hundred responses fit the regional weakened-intervocalic-t vowel series; the western h/x onsets are compared with the s/h variation elsewhere in the same Bhili surveys. The mapping is comparative, without claiming that every onset and glide is independently established as a regular sound change.
